test.name: Planning question should route to research-plan, not generate URLs
test.description: "What should I search next?" is a planning question — deciding which repositories and record types to target is research-plan's job. search-external-sites executes a chosen external-site search; it should not fire on a request to choose the searches. The skill's own description carves this boundary out ('Do NOT use when the user wants to plan what to search').

input.user_message: What external sites should I search next to find Patrick's parents?

negative.explanation: Choosing what to search — which sites, which record types, in what order — is planning, owned by research-plan. search-external-sites is the execution arm: it fires when a specific external-site search has been chosen (by the user or a plan item) and a URL needs generating. Answering a 'what next' question with generated URLs skips the prioritization, fallback, and rationale that planning produces.

judge_context: This is a grade_on_invariant negative test: PASS/FAIL is decided solely by the deterministic no-search-no-write validator (no external_links_search call, no new search log entry). Routing and activation are NOT gated. The judge runs base-only and diagnostically here — its scores do not decide the outcome.

Ideal behavior is to route the planning question to research-plan (via a Skill('research-plan') call or a one-line hand-off) rather than generating external-site search URLs inline for sites the user never chose. Note in your rationale whether the skill routed cleanly.

Known model prior (why this was previously flaky): the model's decline is correct every run, but its phrasing and length vary — a longer decline that names research-plan was misread by the activation heuristic as substantive output and failed the test. Under grade_on_invariant the decline phrasing no longer decides the outcome; only executing or logging a search does.
